goals.description: Harness Forge Session Goal Harness [harness-forge-session] — compiled from capabilities/harnesses/mh-02-harness-forge-session.yaml
goals.gate: All gates passed or degraded-with-log; zero unresolved halt gates, zero stop events

gates.name: 0.1 Startup phrase spoken and forge target pinned: new harness_i
gates.description: Startup phrase spoken and forge target pinned: new harness_id, session_type, and destination path artifacts/harnesses/<id>.yaml declared before any YAML is written
gates.command: Session log line 'TARGET: artifacts/harnesses/<id>.yaml'; id matches /^mh?-[A-Z]?[0-9]{2}-[a-z0-9-]+$/ via python3 regex assertion

gates.name: 0.2 Canonical section contract loaded: the five mandatory sectio
gates.description: Canonical section contract loaded: the five mandatory sections (identity_lock, capability_gates, definition_of_done, failure_protocol, self_improvement) plus envelope fields are recited in the preamble
gates.command: Session preamble contains all five section names verbatim; checked by python3 assertion against the preamble text

gates.name: 0.3 RIG coordinate stated before first file is opened
gates.description: RIG coordinate stated before first file is opened
gates.command: Session log line of form 'COORD: L3-L4 x D1-D3 x A1/A2 x IQRSQPI'

gates.name: 0.4 Harness tuple H_harnessforge(session_type, five_sections, ga
gates.description: Harness tuple H_harnessforge(session_type, five_sections, gates, proof_density, certification) declared with all five components named
gates.command: Session log contains the tuple declaration verbatim

gates.name: 1.1 YAML parses and envelope is complete: harness_id, harness_na
gates.description: YAML parses and envelope is complete: harness_id, harness_name, session_type, coordinate_space (levels/diamonds/bms_modes/iqrsqpi_steps), harness_tuple, bms_bias all present and non-empty
gates.command: python3 -c using yaml.safe_load asserting all envelope keys exist and coordinate_space has its four sub-keys; exit 0 recorded to .rig/forge/envelope.txt

gates.name: 1.2 Five canonical sections present in canonical order: identity
gates.description: Five canonical sections present in canonical order: identity_lock, capability_gates, definition_of_done, failure_protocol, self_improvement
gates.command: python3 -c asserting list(yaml.safe_load(f).keys()) contains the five names and their index order is ascending; output saved to .rig/forge/sections.txt

gates.name: 1.3 identity_lock well-formed: startup_phrase is a first-person
gates.description: identity_lock well-formed: startup_phrase is a first-person sentence and 3-5 gates each carry id and requirement
gates.command: python3 assertion: 3 <= len(identity_lock.gates) <= 5 and every gate has non-empty 'id' and 'requirement'; recorded to .rig/forge/identity.txt

gates.name: 2.1 Capability gate count in band: 8-15 gates total across categ
gates.description: Capability gate count in band: 8-15 gates total across categories; no category empty; every gate carries id, requirement, proof, failure_tier
gates.command: python3 -c flattening capability_gates and asserting 8 <= count <= 15 and all four fields present per gate; count printed to .rig/forge/gate-count.txt

gates.name: 2.2 Every proof names an executable check: each proof string con
gates.description: Every proof names an executable check: each proof string contains at least one command-shaped token (python3, bash, git, grep, ls, exit code assertion) — no proof may be pure prose
gates.command: python3 -c asserting every proof matches /(python3|bash|git|grep|ls|exit|sha256|diff)/; violations printed one per line; zero violations required for exit 0

gates.name: 2.3 Failure tiers are closed-world: every gate's failure_tier is
gates.description: Failure tiers are closed-world: every gate's failure_tier is exactly one of halt/degrade/stop, and failure_protocol.halt_gates/degrade_gates/stop_gates partition the capability gate ids with no orphans and no unknowns
gates.command: python3 -c computing set equality between declared tiers and protocol lists; symmetric difference must be empty; result in .rig/forge/tier-partition.txt

gates.name: 2.4 Refutation probe on proof executability: at least two forged
gates.description: Refutation probe on proof executability: at least two forged proofs are actually executed against the live repo during the forge session and return their claimed shape
gates.command: Each probed proof's real command output saved to .rig/forge/proof-probe-<n>.txt with exit code; a proof whose command errors for environmental reasons must be rewritten, not waived

gates.name: 3.1 MathExec substrate proven live this session: the forged harn
gates.description: MathExec substrate proven live this session: the forged harness's own mathexec-invocing gate (present per the meta-harness contract) is exercised against the real substrate
gates.command: python3 ~/Developer/needle-haystack/artifacts/meta/mathexec_substrate.py self-test exits 0 with 'SELF-TEST PASS'; AND the forged harness contains at least one gate proof referencing mathexec_substrate.py (grep -c >= 1 on the forged file); both recorded to .rig/forge/mathexec.txt

gates.name: 3.2 Memory surface present and live: the forged harness contains
gates.description: Memory surface present and live: the forged harness contains at least one gate requiring a rig-memory-os event recording, and the forge session itself records its event
gates.command: grep -c 'memory.record_event' on forged file >= 1; rig-memory-os memory.record_event(kind="harness_forged", harness=<id>, gates=<n>, certified=<bool>) returns an event id recalled byte-for-byte; round-trip in .rig/forge/memory-roundtrip.txt

gates.name: 4.1 final_rule present and closing: final_rule is a list of 3+ r
gates.description: final_rule present and closing: final_rule is a list of 3+ rules and its last element ends with the exact phrase 'leaves the system stronger than it found it.'
gates.command: python3 -c asserting final_rule[-1].endswith('leaves the system stronger than it found it.'); exit 0 recorded

gates.name: 4.2 Certification pass via harness refuter shape: the forged har
gates.description: Certification pass via harness refuter shape: the forged harness is self-checked for theater gates — no requirement uses unverifiable adjectives ('appropriate', 'sufficient', 'good') without a numeric or executable anchor
gates.command: python3 -c scanning all requirement strings against a banned-bare-adjective list; hits listed in .rig/forge/theater-scan.txt; zero hits for exit 0

gates.name: 4.3 File landed and registered: artifacts/harnesses/<id>.yaml ex
gates.description: File landed and registered: artifacts/harnesses/<id>.yaml exists on disk, parses, and harness_catalog.json is updated (or an explicit catalog-update handoff is recorded)
gates.command: ls and yaml.safe_load succeed on the final path; catalog diff or handoff note saved to .rig/forge/registration.txt

preconditions.startup_phrase: I am the forge. Every gate I write must name its executable proof or it does not exist.
preconditions.bms_bias: A1 verification-led — every forged gate's proof is executed, not read; A2 for prose drafting of requirements; A3 forbidden for proof strings; A4 forbidden — a forged harness is inert until certified

self_improvement.update_trigger: same forge gate fails 3+ times → the forge checklist absorbs the check as a template constraint; recurring theater-gate shapes are proposed via memory.propose_memory to meta-harness-refuter's taxonomy

success_conditions: All gates passed or degraded-with-log; zero unresolved halt gates, zero stop events
Forged YAML parses with complete envelope, five canonical sections, 8-15 fully-fielded gates
Tier partition between gate failure_tier fields and failure_protocol lists proven by set equality
At least one mathexec gate and one memory.record_event gate present in the forged harness and both exercised live
final_rule closes with the required phrase
harness_forged event recorded to rig-memory-os and verified by round-trip recall
One improvement entry appended to the improvements log
failure_states: No stop gates in forge: a malformed harness is simply not registered; the failure mode is refusal to certify, never emergency halt — but 2.3 (tier partition mismatch) invalidates any prior certification of the same file and requires re-running 4.x
halt gate(s) 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3: no progress without gate evidence
